A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MIP attack study despite the changed title and formatting. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, figures, tables, and system prompts, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack-success experiments in Windows Agent Arena, including targeted attacks and transfer across prompts, screenshots, parsers, execution steps, and VLMs (Section 5 and appendix Tables 9–10).

after.justification: v2 retains original MIP attack-success experiments in Section 4 and appendix Tables 8–9. These remain original empirical results even where their values are unchanged from v1.

M1.justification: v2 Section 3.2 adds conditional handling to the stated optimization procedure: replacing image content when a fixed patch intersects parser boxes, periodically checking for intersections, and rolling back with small random perturbations after violations. The recovery mechanism reportedly never activated. The core objective, PGD optimization, and stopping criterion remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Windows Agent Arena task domains, desktop and Bluesky screenshot collections, two malicious target behaviors, and encounters after benign execution steps. Newly cited benchmarks and attack scenarios are not additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: No named competing attack is added to the reported experiments. The same OmniParser and GroundingDINO/TesseractOCR configurations and four Llama Vision variants remain evaluated. New discussions of other attacks do not introduce experimental baseline comparisons.

E3.justification: The listed held-out Notepad prompt drops the explicit output restriction '(and nothing else)' between v1 Table 6 and v2 Table 5, a small reported evaluation-input revision. The PDFs do not establish a rerun. Splits, model configurations, attack budgets, metrics, and the four temperatures documented in the appendix remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Reported temperature-sensitivity evidence is reduced for targeted attacks and execution-step transfer: v2 omits their intermediate-temperature results at 0.1 and 0.5. Full temperature analyses for universal attacks, parser transfer, and VLM transfer remain in the appendix. The added defense discussion contains no new robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the five-output sampling description, five random seeds for the execution-step study, and the same mean-plus/minus reporting practice. Neither adds confidence intervals, significance tests, or an explanation of the uncertainty statistic.

E6.justification: Matched endpoint results and the full appendix matrices are numerically unchanged. Some targeted and execution-step entries disappear, including the desktop website-target ASR of 0.60 ± 0.40 at temperature 0.5 for unseen prompts in v1 Table 1. v2's added zero-ASR rows redisplay the previously reported failure on unseen screenshots.

T1.justification: Equations 1–2 retain the same allowable perturbations, objective, and constraints. Changes to dimension symbols, VLM parameter notation, and the API mapping are equivalent notation. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is added.

C1.justification: The central MIP vulnerability and generalization claims remain. However, v2 removes the blanket assertion that no scientific studies address image-based OS-agent attacks. It also strengthens v1's speculative self-propagation discussion into a claimed 'first demonstration of an OS agent computer worm' in Section 5, without a corresponding propagation experiment.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands applicability and mechanism discussion. It makes use of an optimized VLM a necessary attack condition, replacing v1's softer optimal-effectiveness wording; explains purported advantages of directly encoding programs over indirect steering; and adds image-preprocessing defenses and their robustness–task-performance tradeoff. Appendix A.1 also adds concrete restrictions on end-user deployment.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix A.2 newly discloses an eight-A100 node and approximately 300 node hours for evaluation, and Appendix A.6 updates the stated code/data repository address. Adam hyperparameters, patch dimensions, perturbation limits, optimization-step counts, and the complete system prompt are retained, sometimes relocated.

R1.justification: The research positioning is substantially revised. v1 emphasizes Bailey and Fu and claims an absence of image-based OS-agent studies; v2 identifies Wu et al.'s Dissecting Adversarial Robustness of Multimodal LM Agents as closest, distinguishing direct program induction from caption-mediated attacks. It also incorporates Agent Smith, WASP, and newer transfer-attack work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and discussion receive extensive rewriting. The standalone dangers section is incorporated into the introduction, target programs and optimizer details move into the appendix, and the appendix is reorganized into eight sections. The title and author information also change.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, extensively repositioning and resizing existing displays. Universal-attack and parser-transfer summaries are merged, main tables are condensed to endpoint temperatures, and unseen conditions receive gray shading. All seven figures remain, with revised placement, captions, and some labels.

improvement.justification: v2 improves method and resource documentation, clarifies VLM-specific limitations, and gives more explicit comparisons with related attacks. However, it elevates v1's future self-propagation idea into a claimed first OS-agent-worm demonstration while retaining only the same two evaluated malicious programs. This weakens claim calibration, and some temperature-sensitivity evidence is omitted. The balance between these documentation gains and evidential weaknesses does not support a reliable net quality judgment.
